english.title: Impersonate / make a statement / do an act to falsely suggesting you were a stopping officer
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to deceive

(A)_[impersonated]_
(B)_[made a statement calculated falsely to suggest that you were]_
(C)_[did an act calculated falsely to suggest that you were]_

a stopping officer appointed by the Secretary of State under section 66B of the Road Traffic Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66C(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
with intent to deceive impersonated OR

a stopping officer appointed by the Sec of State under s. 66B RTA 1988

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence was inserted into the Road Traffic Act 1988 by regulation 2 of the Road Vehicles (Powers to Stop) Regulations 2011. S.I. 2011 / 996 refers.
english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..), with intent to deceive, the defendant

(B)_[made a statement calculated falsely to suggest that they were]_
(C)_[did an act calculated falsely to suggest that they were]_

a stopping officer appointed by the Secretary of State under section 66B of the Road Traffic Act 1988.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
